'''Yang-Hui He''' ({{zh|t=何楊輝|s=何杨辉|p=Hé Yáng Huī}}; born 29 September 1975<ref>{{cite web| url=http://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/hey/cv.pdf|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Yang-Hui He|access-date=12 September 2023}}</ref>) is a [[mathematical physicist]], who is a Fellow at the [[London Institute for Mathematical Sciences|London Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yang-Hui He|url=https://lims.ac.uk/profile/?id=102|access-date=2021-10-05|website=LIMS - London Institute for Mathematical Sciences|language=en}}</ref> which is based at the [[Royal Institution of Great Britain]], as well as lecturer and former Fellow at [[Merton College, Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Yang-Hui He|url=https://www.merton.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-yang-hui-he|access-date=2021-10-05|website=Merton College, Oxford}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Yang-Hui He|url=https://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/our-people/he|access-date=2021-10-05|website=University of Oxford Department of Physics|language=en}}</ref> He holds honorary positions as visiting [[professor]] of mathematics at [[City, University of London]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-31|title=Professor Yang-Hui He {{!}} City, University of London|url=https://www.city.ac.uk/about/people/academics/yang-hui-he|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.city.ac.uk|language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Changjiang Scholars|Chang-Jiang Chair professor]] at [[Nankai University]],<ref>{{Cite web | title = Professor He, Chair Professor, Nankai| url=https://zhikuyun.lwinst.com/Liems/web/expert/detail.htm?id=900214886074679331 |website=www.nankai.edu.cn}}</ref> and President of STEMM Global scientific society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=STEMM Global|url=https://stemm.global/|website=stemm.global|access-date=2021-10-07|archive-date=2021-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007135408/https://stemm.global/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Yang works on the interface between [[quantum field theory]], [[string theory]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[number theory]], as well as how [[AI]] and [[machine-learning]] help with these problems.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|last=Lu|first=Donna|title=AI is helping tackle one of the biggest unsolved problems in maths|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2226493-ai-is-helping-tackle-one-of-the-biggest-unsolved-problems-in-maths/|access-date=2021-10-05|website=New Scientist|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hutson|first=Matthew|title=Companies make it easier for scientists to use AI | url=https://www.science.org/content/article/no-coding-required-companies-make-it-easier-ever-scientists-use-artificial-intelligence|access-date=2021-10-05|website=Science Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref> He is one of the pioneers of the field of using AI for pure mathematics.

Yang is author of over 200 scientific publications<ref>{{Cite web | title = Yang-Hui He Publications | url = https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=I5SWIuoAAAAJ&hl=en | website = www.scholar.google.com}}</ref> and is also a keen communicator of science, giving regular public lectures<ref>{{Cite web |title=ToE | website=[[YouTube]] | date=24 February 2022 | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=llGvkEgXnAQ }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Universes as Big Data | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=feGuGLTUziI&t=924s | website=Youtube| date=27 November 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-05-09|title=Muß Es Sein? – Epigraph to a String Quartet|url=https://icmsnews.wordpress.com/2014/05/09/mus-es-sein-epigraph-to-a-string-quartet/|access-date=2021-10-11|website=ICMS NEWS|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=慕校|url=http://nk.umlink.cn/Moos/nankai/mobile/index.html?shareProfileId=|access-date=2021-10-11|website=nk.umlink.cn}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=In conversation with Sir Roger Penrose|url=https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/events-2021/october/public-in-conversation-with-sir-roger-penrose|access-date=2021-10-12|website=www.rigb.org|language=en|archive-date=2021-10-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211005120943/https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/events-2021/october/public-in-conversation-with-sir-roger-penrose|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title = The DIAS Statutory Public Lecture| date = 5 December 2024| url=https://www.dias.ie/2024/11/01/stp-statutory-public-lecture-5-december-2024-prof-yang-hui-he/}}</ref>  including the Royal Institution Friday Evening Discourse,<ref>{{Cite web |title = Geometry and Physics | date=24 February 2023| url=https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/how-geometry-created-modern-physics-discourse}}</ref> 
as well as podcasts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Muss es Sein? | url=https://www.knowitwall.com/episodes/string-theory-must-it-be-so/|website=Know it all Wall}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The 23 Challenges| url=https://onegarden.com/talk/rethinking-maths| website=onegarden.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Paradigm interview | url=https://open.spotify.com/episode/3GOKMe3JGfCmgTuFts5A5W?go=1&sp_cid=74349a32e3fca08ea1adbbc74a8fa582&nd=1|website=Machine-Learning the universe}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fidyas Interview: Dialogues with Roger Penrose | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mJpjaUNXC-Y|website=AI, Consciousness and Maths| date=28 April 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Curt Jaimungal ToE Interview: How Maths is changed | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wbP0KjWm0pw|website=Maths is changed forever| date=2 January 2025 }}</ref>
His other outreach activities include acting as an advisor to BMUCO<ref>{{Cite web|title=BMUCO, a student NGO for outreach| url=
https://mobile.twitter.com/bmuco_org/status/1358734100828364807| website=www.bmuco.org}}</ref> and being a fellow of the One Garden.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OneGarden| url=https://onegarden.com/fellow/dr-yang-hui-he| website=onegarden.com}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Yang received his [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] in [[Physics]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1996, with Highest Honours (''[[summa cum laude]]'', [[Allen Shenstone]] Prize and Kusaka Memorial Prize), joint with certificates in applied mathematics and in engineering physics. He received his [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Masters]] from [[University of Cambridge]] in 1997 with Distinction and then obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 2002 in the [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]] ([[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Scholarship and MIT Presidential Award) under the supervision of Amihay Hanany.<ref>
{{Cite web|title=Yang-Hui He - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=68908|access-date=2021-10-05|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

After postdoctoral work at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], in the group of [[Burt Ovrut]], Yang joined the [[University of Oxford]] as [[Richard FitzJames|FitzJames Fellow]] and Advanced Fellow of the [[STFC]], UK, working closely with [[Philip Candelas]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ananthaswamy|first=Anil|title=String Theory may Predict the Universe|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg19726370-100-string-theory-may-predict-our-universe-after-all/?ignored=irrelevant/|access-date=2021-10-05|website=New Scientist|language=en-US}}</ref> He remains a tutor at [[Merton College | Merton College, Oxford]] when taking up his professorships at the University of London and Nankai University, and more recently, when he joined the [[London Institute for Mathematical Sciences|London Institute]].

== Works ==

Yang has authored over 200 journal papers,<ref>{{Cite web | title = Yang-Hui He Publications | url = https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=I5SWIuoAAAAJ&hl=en | website = www.scholar.google.com}}</ref> as well as several books, notably:

* ''Topology and Physics'',<ref>{{Cite book | title = Topology and Physics | year = 2019 | doi = 10.1142/11217 | last1 = Yang | first1 = Chen Ning | last2 = Ge | first2 = Mo-Lin | last3 = He | first3 = Yang-Hui | isbn = 978-981-327-849-3 | s2cid = 125570349 |publisher=World Scientific}}</ref> co-edited with [[C. N. Yang]] and Mo-Lin Ge, with contributions from [[Sir Michael Atiyah]], [[Edward Witten]], [[Sir Roger Penrose]], [[Robbert Dijkgraaf]] et al., recommended by Book Authority as one of the 20 most influential books in quantum field theory of all time.<ref>{{Cite web| title = best QFT books| url = https://bookauthority.org/books/best-quantum-field-theory-books| access-date = 2023-04-30| archive-date = 2023-04-30| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20230430084039/https://bookauthority.org/books/best-quantum-field-theory-books| url-status = dead}}</ref>
* ''The Calabi-Yau Landscape: from geometry, to physics, to machine-learning'',<ref>{{Cite journal | title = The Calabi-Yau Landscape | year = 2021 | url = https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783030775612 | website = www.springer.com}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02893 arXiv preprint]</ref> textbook aimed at early PhD students, introducing mathematics to physicists, physics to mathematicians and machine-learning to both, the first textbook on the AI mathematician.
* ''Dialogues Between Physics and Mathematics: C. N. Yang at 100'',<ref>{{Cite book | title = Dialogues Between Physics and Mathematics | year = 2022 | url = https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-17523-7 | publisher = www.springer.com| doi = 10.1007/978-3-031-17523-7 | isbn = 978-3-031-17522-0 | s2cid = 254556368 | editor-last1 = Ge | editor-last2 = He | editor-first1 = Mo-Lin | editor-first2 = Yang-Hui }}</ref> co-edited with Mo-Lin Ge, with contributions from [[Edward Witten]], [[Sir Roger Penrose]], [[Sir Anthony James Leggett]], [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Alexander Polyakov]], [[Vladimir Drinfeld]] et al., celebrating the 100th birthday of [[C. N. Yang]].
* ''Machine Learning in Pure Mathematics and Theoretical Physics'',<ref>{{Cite book | title = ML math-physics | date=2023 | doi=10.1142/q0404 | url = https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/q0404#t=aboutBook | last1=He | first1=Yang-Hui | isbn=978-1-80061-369-0 | s2cid=251971587 }}</ref> the first of its kind, as a collection of essays on the interactions between AI and pure mathematics/fundamental physics.
